notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already used up when this part began (the first search was refused: 200 of 200 used), so none of these thirty candidates could be searched for. Everything below was found by opening pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed: the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (learned by running the kit's own step, python -m ballot.local_sites files, on a scratch copy of the database; each was then opened and read), each government's own site, the two state parties' and local party units' own sites, the Legislative Reference Library, the University of Minnesota's election archive, and a few news sites. No search engine was read in place of the search tool. A second pass with searching would be worth it for the candidates with nothing below.

Nothing citable was found for Julian Rodriguez, Derek Armstrong, Christian Kirmeier, Sarah Phan-Budd, Peter Hardy, Chad Moser and the two judges (Matthew Schmidt, Stephanie L. Beckman); Emily Christie has a review item only. The judges: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site and the Governor's pages were not requested, because other parts of this sweep had already found that they refuse scripts (a 403 or a Cloudflare check; a CAPTCHA), and no other page naming either judge could be reached without searching. The City of Shakopee's own list of candidates names Julian Rodriguez and gives no website for him. The Glencoe-Silver Lake district's own "Meet the GSL School Board Candidates" page carries Chad Moser's answers, which name no public office and no website (what they say of work and household is not recorded). The Hibbing district's and city's pages do not name Peter Hardy; Monticello's council and commission pages do not name Derek Armstrong; Winona's council and commission pages do not name Sarah Phan-Budd, and the Winona Journal's own site search finds nothing on that race.

Not read, and nothing worked around: columbiaheightsmn.gov and ci.sauk-rapids.mn.us (their robots.txt asks scripts to stay out, so Rachel James has no official page here and her council service rests on her own campaign site, and nothing could be checked for Christian Kirmeier); 5il.co, a document host one school district links to (robots.txt); slcgop.org (it leads to a social media page); the Senate District 8 Republicans, whose only web presence on the 8th Congressional District Republicans' list of local units is a social media page; martincountygop.com (404) and wrightcountyrepublicans.com (402).

James Tacheny's campaign site (the address the Senate District 44 Republicans publish for him) could not be read by the kit's reader on this machine: Python refused its certificate ("self-signed certificate in certificate chain"), over https and http alike. Certificate checking was not turned off. The page was read with the fetch tool instead, which reported the sentence quoted in his entry (twice, the same both times) but gave the page's title two ways, so no title is quoted; the second reader should open the site in a browser. Until the certificate is sorted out the kit's fetch step will record this site as not answering, so no photo options or issue headings will come from it.

Endorsements: the Minnesota DFL's own list names Daniel Horoshak (House District 7B), Dan Wilson (26A) and Leigh Finke (66A); the Winona County DFL's home page lists Dan Wilson among "the candidates who are endorsed in the 2026 Elections"; the Senate District 45 Republicans' "Endorsed Candidates" page calls Andrew Myers "our endorsed Republican candidate to retain the House District 45A seat". No party page that uses the word endorsed was found for Darrick Law (the 8th Congressional District Republicans list him under "2026 Candidates") or James Tacheny (the Senate District 44 Republicans list him under "REPUBLICAN PARTY CANDIDATES"), so neither has an endorsed_by entry.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape other parts use): the Senate District 31 Republicans' 2026 Voting Guide names Brian Kirkham under "Recommended Nonpartisan Candidates", a heading that is not the word endorsement, so it is kept apart from endorsed_by and no page should call it an endorsement; whether and how it is shown is John's decision.

Sitting legislators (Andrew Myers, Leigh Finke): the website, the party's endorsement, and what the Legislative Reference Library adds to the roster, which is Finke's birth date (the roster has none) and Myers's three local posts (the roster already has his birth date, and the Library's matches it). No review items: the Library's dates of service agree with the roster.

Dan Wilson's birth year is from the Minnesota Historical Election Archive (University of Minnesota Libraries). It is a university archive, not a news organization, and is labelled secondary for the second reader to judge; the sources it names for him are the Secretary of State's candidate filings, his campaign website and the Winona Journal, not a birth records index. The Winona Journal of August 4, 2025 gives his age as 37, which fits. The archive has no page under the names tried for Darrick Law, James Tacheny or Dan Horoshak.

Jay Maynard: Wikipedia's article on him gives a birth date with no citation attached, so no birth year is recorded. The City of Fairmont's Charter Commission page lists "James R. Maynard, III" among its appointees; no page read ties that name to Jay Maynard in so many words, so the commission seat rests on his own campaign site. That site's About page reads as written before he joined the council, and the city's Board of Zoning Appeals page does not list him today; both posts are recorded without dates.

Emily Christie: the review item rests on a news organization (the Sun Current, hometownsource.com), not on an official source. That site's robots.txt allows the kit's User-Agent but turns away several AI crawlers by name, Anthropic's among them; one article was read there and nothing else is taken from it. The same is true of two front pages that were read and not used (mesabitribune.com, willmarradio.com); a third, swnewsmedia.com, turns away other companies' AI crawlers. Whether such sites should be read at all is John's call.

Dave Dunn: the Waseca district's School Board page names him only in the caption of the board's photo; his seat and title come from the list that page links, "2026 Waseca School Board of Education Members", a document the district keeps on Google Docs (read as plain text; only names, titles and terms were looked at). David Marquardt and Dave Dunn: the Moorhead and Waseca district sites draw their pages by script, so a script finds the names inside the page's data, and a browser shows them on the page.

Two official pages print a home address beside the office holder's name, so they are not the pages cited here: Blue Earth County's own page about Kevin Paap (https://www.blueearthcountymn.gov/1567/Kevin-Paap, which also carries his portrait and "Served Since: 2021") and Watonwan County's County Officials table (https://www.co.watonwan.mn.us/121/County-Officials). The pages cited instead (Blue Earth County's Board of Commissioners table; Watonwan County's Human Services Board members) give the same facts without an address. Whether to link to the other two is John's decision.

Not recorded: staff jobs in government that two candidates' own sites describe (jobs, not public offices), and the party posts two other sites mention (not public offices either). Brad Canham's "Member of Governor's WorkForce Council" is recorded as his site lists it, with no years; the second reader may judge whether it was an appointed seat or part of a job.

Addresses tried and dropped, because nothing on them ties them to these races: christiankirmeier.com (not a campaign site), phanbudd.com and julianrodriguez.com (empty), emilychristie.com (a holding page), electchristie.com (it leads to another person's campaign elsewhere).

Second reader (2026-10-02): every address in this file was opened again with the kit's honest User-Agent (James Tacheny's site with the fetch tool, since Python still refuses its certificate). Kept as recorded, with small wording corrections where a claim could not be seen again: the 8th Congressional District Republicans' and Senate District 44 Republicans' pages are named in the notes without addresses, so the website entries no longer lean on them; Bobby Lambert's About-page timeline was not re-read. Removed: Brad Canham's own_words and his Governor's WorkForce Council entry (see "removed"). Dan Wilson's birth year stays labelled secondary: the University of Minnesota archive is neither Wikipedia nor a news organization, though the Winona Journal's age for him agrees; John may prefer to leave it out. Emily Christie's review item rests on a news report, not an official source, and is kept labelled as such. Dan Horoshak's own_words is a party post in his own words; the sentence around it on his site names a union, an employer and other memberships, none of which is recorded.
